issuer.summary: No holder can force their own exit — redemption is a queue the operator chooses to process. That is the issuer question for a credit product, and it is deliberately scored identically for syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT because it is a fact about Maple rather than about either pool. Maple Labs is a Cayman entity with a doxxed team, more than eight audits, a $1M bug bounty and roughly a three-year clean operating record on the Syrup line, which is a stronger track record than most of this corpus and is what holds the score at the middle of the range. What sits against it is the shape of the discretion the operator holds. Withdrawals run through a processed queue rather than an entitlement, so the pool delegate can decline to process, and the authority that does it carries a threshold of one. Above that, protocol governance runs through a 3-day timelock at a threshold of two — and those are the same two keys that govern the sibling pool, not an equivalent pair, so the two products do not provide independent governance. A holder is therefore trusting Maple's conduct rather than a mechanism that constrains it, and the track record is the reason that has been a reasonable trade so far. Nothing here is hidden or unusual for institutional private credit; it is simply discretion rather than a guarantee, and the axis prices it as such.

facts: ⚠️ THE EXIT IS DISCRETIONARY. Redemption is a PROCESSED QUEUE, not an entitlement — no holder can force their own way out, and the pool delegate can decline to process. The authority that does it carries THRESHOLD 1.

⚠️ Protocol governance runs via governor -> GovernorTimelock at 3 days, THRESHOLD 2 — and it is the SAME TWO KEYS that govern syrupUSDT, not an equivalent pair. The two Syrup products do not provide independent governance.
✅ Maple Labs (Cayman), doxxed team, 8+ audits, $1M bug bounty, and roughly a three-year clean operating record on the Syrup product line — a stronger track record than most of this corpus.

⚠️ THIS AXIS SCORES THE ENTITY, so it is IDENTICAL for syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT — Maple curates both. Per-asset differences (different pools, different collateral mixes) belong on Structural and legitimately differ there.
⚠️ The recorded defeat condition for this asset's authority model is 'governance-role-capture-2-eoas' — two externally-owned keys, which is the same count as the governance threshold.

⚠️ NOT priced here and stated to prevent double-counting: the loan book's composition, the collateral mix and the Loans/Liquidity split are Backing and Structural facts. This axis prices the OPERATOR's discretion and record.

⚠️ PROCESS NOTE, kept because it explains a past divergence: this score was published for both Syrup assets with nothing upstream holding it, so syrup_family_analyzer.py borrowed structural_score (6.5 / 6.0) and emitted it into a field named issuer_score — overriding the authored 5.5 on two live public surfaces. tidresearch remains the authoring surface for both.
